extraction.name: Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images
extraction.description: A dataset of millions of tiny color images collected from the web, including labeled subsets CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 for object recognition experiments.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.citeAs: Krizhevsky, A. (2009). Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Groups at MIT and NYU collected a dataset of millions of tiny color images from the web by searching for images of every non-abstract English noun in the lexical database WordNet using several search engines including Google, Flickr, and Alta vista. They kept roughly the first 3000 results for each search term. After collecting, they removed perfect duplicates and images with an excessively large portion of white pixels. For the labeled subsets (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100), students were paid to label images by filtering out mislabeled images based on specific criteria.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Millions of tiny color images downloaded from the web via search engines (Google, Flickr, Alta vista) for nouns in WordNet.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Over the span of six months
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were downscaled to 32x32. Perfect duplicates and images with excessive white pixels were removed. For the labeled subsets, duplicate images were removed by comparing images with the L2 norm. The data was also subjected to ZCA whitening transformation and deletion of the 1000 least significant principal components in some experiments.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were downscaled to 32x32. ZCA whitening transformation was applied. In some experiments, the 1000 least significant directions of variance were deleted. For training RBMs on patches, 32x32 images were segmented into 25 8x8 patches plus one globally subsampled 8x8 patch.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Students were paid to label a subset of the dataset. They were assigned a class and asked to examine images found with that class or its hyponyms as search terms. They were instructed to reject images that did not belong to the assigned class based on criteria such as: the class name should be a likely answer to 'What is in this picture?', the image should be photo-realistic (reject line drawings), and contain only one prominent instance of the object. The authors personally verified every label submitted.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The search terms used to find images provide rough labels, but they are extremely unreliable due to the nature of online image search technology. The dataset contains only about 3000 images per search term.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The original dataset had no reliable class labels, making it hard to use for object recognition experiments without manual labeling. The search terms provided unreliable rough labels. The dataset is biased towards objects that can be easily searched for by noun in WordNet.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Unsupervised training of deep generative models, object recognition experiments, training and testing classification models.
